metadata.title: Amsterdam chapter
metadata.description: Free courses and a weekly discussion group across UvA, VU Amsterdam, and the city's tech scene, supported by ELLIS Unit Amsterdam.

hero.subheading: Free courses and a weekly discussion group across UvA, VU Amsterdam, and the city's tech scene, supported by ELLIS Unit Amsterdam.

hero.caption: Amsterdam, where the courses run on site

programs.heading: Two free courses run in Amsterdam

technical.intro: Curious where your technical skills could make the biggest difference for AI safety?
technical.body: SAIN Amsterdam facilitates the <bluedot>BlueDot Impact</bluedot> <course>Technical AI Safety</course> course for people who want to help close the gap between how fast AI capabilities are advancing and how well we can make them safe. Over six weeks, you’ll diagnose why building safe AI is so technically hard, evaluate current safety techniques (what works, what doesn’t, and where the gaps are), and map how defences might break by building your own “kill chain”. You’ll leave with a fundable action plan for where your skills can make the biggest difference. SAIN Amsterdam supports ambitious students in finding their next steps in an AI safety career.
technical.background: Technical understanding is ideal, but not a prerequisite. This is a foundational course, covering the foundations of technical AI safety.

governance.intro: What would it take to govern technology that is advancing faster than the rules meant to guide it?
governance.body: SAIN Amsterdam facilitates the <bluedot>BlueDot Impact</bluedot> <course>Frontier AI Governance</course> course, which helps you build the judgment to shape how frontier AI is governed. Over six weeks, you’ll assess the evidence, compare competing strategies, and test your ideas through practical exercises and group discussion, leaving with a concrete plan for how you can contribute. Because the course leans heavily on US and China perspectives, our facilitators are encouraged to also bring in European and Dutch materials. Whatever your background, Safe AI Netherlands is here to help you take your next step toward a career in AI safety.
governance.background: No governance background needed. This is a foundational course that builds up the core ideas of AI governance step by step.

courses.note: The courses are independently run by SAIN Amsterdam and are not affiliated with UvA or VU. The certificate of completion is awarded by SAIN Amsterdam, not BlueDot Impact.

programs.discussionGroup: A weekly discussion group on technical AI safety reads and discusses current research; about two hours a session, guided by experienced mentors.
programs.research: Members also run research projects, currently including work on failure modes of multi-agent debate.

team.body: SAIN Amsterdam is directed by Ana Paula Castillo Rodriguez, with a team covering research, education, events, and PR. Formerly AI Safety Amsterdam (AISA), the chapter draws people from BSc students to professionals at companies like Deloitte and Shell, and from independent researchers to ELLIS assistant professors.

record.heading: This already happened in Amsterdam
record.body: The chapter's courses have drawn more than 120 applicants. It has also run a season of weekly discussion groups and presented at the AI020 Conference and TEDxUniversiteit van Amsterdam.

metadata.title: Groningen chapter
metadata.description: Free courses, hackathons, and published research, running in Groningen since 2023. It began as the AI Safety Initiative Groningen (AISIG) and continues as SAIN Groningen.

hero.subheading: Free courses, hackathons, and published research, running in Groningen since 2023. It began as the AI Safety Initiative Groningen (AISIG) and continues as SAIN Groningen.

hero.caption: Groningen, home of the chapter since 2023

programs.heading: Join one of our free courses!

technical.intro: Curious to learn about the technical approaches to AI safety?
technical.body: SAIN Groningen facilitates the <bluedot>BlueDot Impact</bluedot> <course>Technical AI Safety</course> course for people who want to learn about the open problems in technical AI safety and the techniques to address them. It takes six weeks, with about three hours of reading and a two-hour discussion session each week. The discussion sessions are guided by a facilitator, creating the perfect space to both discuss the material and connect with others who are eager to work on AI safety too.

governance.intro: Curious to learn about the governance challenges around AI safety?
governance.body: SAIN Groningen facilitates the <bluedot>BlueDot Impact</bluedot> <course>Frontier AI Governance</course> course, which helps you build the judgment to shape how frontier AI is governed. Since the BlueDot course mainly covers the US and China dynamic, we have extended the curriculum with hand-picked materials on tackling AI safety from the EU’s perspective. The course takes six weeks, with about three hours of reading and a two-hour discussion session each week. The discussion sessions are guided by a facilitator, creating the perfect space to both discuss the materials in detail and connect with others who are eager to work on AI safety too.

programs.footnote: The courses are independently run by SAIN Groningen and are not affiliated with the University of Groningen (RUG). The certificate of completion is awarded by SAIN Groningen, not BlueDot Impact.
programs.discussionGroups: Two discussion groups meet through the year, each with at least one experienced mentor: technical AI alignment (scalable oversight, evaluation and red-teaming, preference learning, robustness, deployment risks) and AI governance and privacy (policies, regulations, accountability, transparency and fairness).

team.body: SAIN Groningen is directed by Tarteel Mohamed, with work organised across four teams: education, events, communications, and research operations; a structure other chapters are adopting as they spin up. The chapter grew out of the AI Safety Initiative Groningen (AISIG), running since 2023.

record.heading: 30 events and counting
record.body: Since October 2023 the chapter has run 30 events: hackathons, course graduations, research talks, pub quizzes, and socials; first as AISIG and, since 30 April 2026, as SAIN Groningen. Members' research has been published at NeurIPS and ICLR workshops.

metadata.title: Utrecht chapter
metadata.description: A free AI safety course, two discussion groups, and a growing research track at Utrecht University. Run by volunteers, open to anyone in the city.

hero.subheading: A free AI safety course, two discussion groups, and a growing research track at Utrecht University. Run by volunteers, open to anyone in the city.
hero.photoAlt: The Dom tower rising over the houses of Utrecht city centre
hero.caption: Utrecht city centre, where the course meets

programs.heading: Three free courses run in Utrecht
programs.openLead: Applications for AI Governance and Technical AI Safety are open.

fundamentals.summary: AI Safety Fundamentals has run three times in Utrecht, reaching more than 100 participants: BSc and MSc students, researchers, engineers, and public-sector staff. Four weeks, one hour of reading and a one-hour lecture a week, at Utrecht University in the city centre. In week four you choose a technical path, a governance path, or both. You get a certificate for attending all sessions; no previous background is needed.

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.detail: High-level overview of AI safety, why it matters now, capabilities and diffusion, types of risks, and solution strategies, technical and governance.

risks.title: Types of risks and incidents
risks.detail: Social harms, frontier risks, misuse, loss of control; real-world cases and how research lags behind deployment.

difficulty.title: Why AI safety is difficult
difficulty.detail: Industry incentives, funding gaps, expert disagreement, slow regulation against fast labs, geopolitical race dynamics.

paths.title: Path specialisation
paths.detail: The fourth week splits in two. Take one path, or both.

technical.title: Technical AI safety
technical.detail: Jailbreaking, the scalable oversight problem, RLHF and reward signals.

governance.title: Governance
governance.detail: Overview of the EU AI Act, accountability in AI systems, international actors in AI safety.

technical.summary: Technical AI Safety is a four-week, in-person course at SAIN Utrecht for people who can program and know the basics of AI. Knowing how transformers work is recommended. Each week covers one area of the field: the first two weeks focus on how AI safety evaluators test models, week three looks at safety in robots and other physical systems, and week four covers securing AI agents. The weekly assignments use material from ARENA, an established AI safety training programme, and especially strong solutions are sent to ARENA for review and may be added to their repository. A workshop every Saturday from 13:00 to 15:00 helps you complete them. After the course, we launch a research challenge where our mentors help you develop your own ideas. Each week has about one hour of reading, one to three hours of assignments and a 1.5-hour lecture.

evaluationsIntro.title: Introduction to AI safety evaluations
evaluationsIntro.detail: What evaluations are and why we need them, capability versus alignment evaluations, and how to design one: threat models, datasets and scoring.

evaluationsInPractice.title: Implementing and evaluating AI safety evaluations
evaluationsInPractice.detail: Running evaluations in practice with tools, understanding the common problems that make results unreliable, and how results are communicated to policymakers.

embodied.title: Embodied AI safety
embodied.detail: The safety risks of robots and other physical AI systems, safety filters, using vision-language models to spot unsafe actions, and measuring uncertainty.

agents.title: Securing AI agents
agents.detail: How agents are attacked through prompt injection and their tools, why model-level defences fail, secure design and AI Control, and how AI can also act as a defender.

governance.summary: AI Governance is a new four-week course at SAIN Utrecht, open to everyone, with no previous background needed. Most AI governance courses focus on the US and China. In this course, we also look at their visions and ambitions and at where middle powers like the EU fit in. We also dedicate an entire lecture to how Europe and the Netherlands are regulating AI. Throughout the course, we read and discuss primary sources, such as government strategies, laws, and documents from AI labs, giving you the tools to follow developments in AI regulation and geopolitics independently. Each week has about one to two hours of reading and a 1.5-hour lecture.

introduction.title: Introduction to AI governance and AI safety
introduction.detail: What AI governance is, how it differs from technical safety, why it matters now, and the main risks: misuse, loss of control, and concentration of power.

geopolitics.title: AI geopolitics
geopolitics.detail: The key actors (governments, labs, safety organisations, the UN), US and Chinese visions and ambitions, and where middle powers fit.

policymakerTools.title: The tools of the policymaker
policymakerTools.detail: Analysis of past incidents like the Hugging Face case, system cards, and future scenarios.

europe.title: Governance in Europe and the Netherlands
europe.detail: The EU AI Act and its gaps, the EU AI Office and the GPAI Code of Practice, the Dutch AI landscape.

programs.footnote: These courses are independently run by SAIN Utrecht and are not affiliated with Utrecht University.
programs.discussionGroups: Between cohorts, two discussion groups keep meeting: one on technical AI safety, currently a mechanistic interpretability reading group, and one on AI governance and policy.
programs.research: The chapter is building a research track: red-teaming language models, safety evaluation, interpretability, and agent behaviour. The Project Hub launches in October 2026.

team.body: SAIN Utrecht is directed by Riccardo Campanella. The team is growing across four areas: education, events, communication, and research. The chapter's work is funded by BERI, with mentorship from Pathfinder.

record.heading: This already happened in Utrecht
record.body: Over the past year the chapter ran the Win4AISafety open research summer challenge, a full technical course with a closing dinner, discussion groups including a Europe 2031 scenario session, and research talks, including an Anthropic researcher speaking to more than 60 people.
